description: A composite EBSD figure laid out as a 3x3 grid of maps acquired prior to deformation; every panel carries a 40 um scale bar. The three columns are, left to right: (a, b, c) inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation maps with a colour-triangle key labelled 001, 101 and 111; (a1, b1, c1) grey-scale IQ (image quality / band contrast) maps; (a2, b2, c2) KAM (kernel average misorientation) maps with a 0-5 colour bar. The rows are the three alloys labelled in-image as Zr0, Zr0.01 and Zr0.50. Zr0 shows equiaxed grains with a broad size distribution and random orientations, its KAM map being almost uniformly dark blue (low misorientation). Zr0.01 shows visibly finer, still randomly oriented grains, with dark spots in the IQ map and a KAM map that is still largely blue with only sparse green speckles. Zr0.50 is strongly heterogeneous: its IQ map reveals vertical bands of fine grains embedded in coarser grain zones, and its KAM map concentrates green (high-misorientation) speckle in exactly those fine-grained bands while the coarse zones stay blue. The figure therefore demonstrates that increasing Zr refines the recrystallised FCC grains and, at 0.50 wt%, generates a bimodal fine/coarse heterostructure whose dislocation density is localised in the fine-grained zones.

subfigures.description: IPF orientation map of the Zr0 steel, 40 um scale bar, colour key with 001/101/111 corners; equiaxed grains with random (multi-coloured) orientations and a broad grain-size distribution.
Grey-scale IQ (image quality) map of Zr0; equiaxed grains outlined by dark boundaries, little internal contrast.
KAM map of Zr0; almost uniformly dark blue across the whole field with a 0-5 colour bar, i.e. uniformly low misorientation.
IPF map of the Zr0.01 steel, 40 um scale bar; grains noticeably finer than Zr0 and still randomly coloured (random orientations).
IQ map of Zr0.01; fine equiaxed grains with several small dark spots whose nature is not identified.
KAM map of Zr0.01; predominantly dark blue with only faint, sparse green speckles.
IPF map of the Zr0.50 steel, 40 um scale bar; heterogeneous grain structure with differently oriented (randomly coloured) grains.
IQ map of Zr0.50; distinct vertical bands of fine grains with dark high-contrast domains embedded in coarser grain regions, giving a bimodal/heterostructured appearance.
KAM map of Zr0.50; blue background with green high-misorientation speckle confined to the vertical fine-grained bands, the coarse zones remaining blue.

observations.observation: The figure is a 3x3 grid of EBSD maps whose rows are labelled in-image Zr0, Zr0.01 and Zr0.50 and whose panels each carry a 40 um scale bar.
The left-column IPF maps are accompanied by a colour-triangle legend whose corners are labelled 001, 101 and 111, indicating a cubic (FCC) orientation key.
The right-column KAM maps use a rainbow colour bar annotated from 0 to 5; the numeric unit of this scale is not printed on the figure.
The Zr0 KAM map (a2) is almost uniformly dark blue, showing low misorientation throughout the mapped area.
The grains in the Zr0.01 IPF map (b) appear visibly finer than those in the Zr0 map (a), while their colours remain randomly distributed.

The Zr0.50 IQ map (c1) shows vertical bands of fine grains alternating with coarser grain regions, and the matching KAM map (c2) places its green high-misorientation speckle only within those fine-grained bands.
The caption states the EBSD data comprise IPF, IQ and KAM maps of Zr-alloyed Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steels prior to deformation, with (a)-(a2) Zr0, (b)-(b2) Zr0.01 and (c)-(c2) Zr0.50.
The citing text states that the Zr0 steel has equiaxed FCC grains with low KAM values.
The citing text states that adding micro-alloyed Zr to the Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steel obviously reduces the average size of recrystallized FCC grains and randomises their orientations (Fig. 2b-b2).

The citing text states that Fig. 2c-c2 shows a distinct heterostructure of CG zones and FG zones, the FG zones having high KAM values that indicate a high density of dislocations decorating the fine FCC grains.
The citing text quotes a value of about 37% for f_CG,b, the fraction of coarse grains adjacent to fine grains, based on the EBSD result in Fig. 2.
No numeric grain size, KAM value or phase fraction is printed on any panel of the figure itself.
